text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Defence forces commander, General Gustav Hagglund, warned that further cuts in defence budget could end refresher training courses and severely limit fly time for Finland's new Hornet fighters.

- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen defended Finland's policy towards Europe's Economic and Monetary Union at Nordic Council meeting in Copenhagen, and called for joint Nordic approach to third stage of EMU. @
- Defunct Finnish Communist Party could be re-registered next year, if drive to collect 5,000 signatures succeeds.
- Finnish Office for Free Competition says European Commission ruling on planned merger of wholesale and retail groups Kesko and Tuko will serve as useful precedent.

- Dispute over fees for passage through inland Saimaa Canal came to a head last week when Russian officials demanded almost 30,000 markka from one Finnish vessel. Foreign ministries now dealing with disagreement. @

- Helsinki ranked third best city in Europe for business people to live -- and 13th best in the world by worldwide Corporate Resources consulting group. Only Geneva and Zurich ranked higher among European cities.
- Representative of the Centre Party of Aland, Olof Salmen appears likely candidate to become next president of Nordic Council when Finland takes over as chair country. @
- Finland's new representatives to European Parliament took their seats in Strasbourg for first time on Monday.
- Private television production company VipVision sold to Danish Egmont Group, which already minority partner in Ruutunelonen, holder of new nationwide commercial TV licence.
- Finnish volunteer group put Martin Luther's works -- over 18,000 pages -- on CD-ROM.
- Bank home loan administration charges make big difference in cost of borrowing. @
- Finnish diversified group Wihuri Oy started joint venture with Japanese Nichimen Corporation to manufacture food packaging films in Lahti.
